correctness.rationale: In zero-sum canonical Euclidean metric on the free-space unit ball, the polar is the centered 1-Lipschitz potential polytope. Verified active tight graph connected iff vertex and two-level signed potential structure with A levels 0,s and B levels 1-t,1, requiring anchors. Norm-square of centered potential is exactly Q(x,y)=q+s²x-(2t-t²)y-(q+sx-ty)²/N. For any nonzero minority count x the submission supplies strict decrease/decrease-both screening, reducing all maximizers to x=0 for p<=q, 0<s,t<1. Then H(j)=pq/N+t(t-2p/N)j-t²j²/N is strictly concave and maximized at clipped nearest integers to N/2-p/t. Corrected polar support radius is 1/sqrt(max H) globally by antipodal facets; contacting polar vertices count 2 sum binom(q,j); their spans have rank one (j=0) or q (j>0), so all-center affine dimension N-2 or p-1. The first tie at t=2p/(N-1) occurs interior only q>=p+2; equality has 2(q+1) contacts. Independent exact rational enumeration of all profile pairs x,y for (p,q)=(2,2),(2,4),(3,5),(4,8) and four heterogeneous (s,t) samples each confirmed strict screening/maxima, beyond the repository independently inspected spanning-tree checker. These finite checks do not prove the real-parameter screening lemma.

value.rationale: A two-nonsingleton-cluster ultrametric with independent internal radii is a natural extension of the already-studied equal-radius model. The non-obvious sharp screening that *all* canonical Euclidean radii and tangent normals ignore minority s, even when s>t, and the complete affine-dimension collapse of all optimal centers are useful structural facts beyond the known diagonal variance staircase. At exact transition the contact count changes sharply; no paper-sized downstream theorem is required for this motivated complete parametric classification.

limitations: The claim is for real scalar potentials, canonical Euclidean coordinates, two internally equilateral clusters with 2<=p<=q and 0<s,t<1 only.
The equal-radius s=t inradius and branch threshold were already prior mathematical results; only extended heterogeneous scope and additional center geometry are considered original.
Best-of-knowledge originality; no claim of exhaustive priority or formal/expert certification.
